properties.name: Solstice Advanced Materials (formerly Honeywell / Allied Chemical) — AWE Superfund Site
properties.source: EPA NPL / NCC Parcel Records (0607400002) / Honeywell-Solstice spin-off Oct. 2025
properties.note: NCC Parcel 0607400002 — 14.72 acres, Allied Corporation subdivision, 0 Off Philadelphia Pike, Claymont. As of Oct. 30, 2025, Honeywell completed the spin-off of its Advanced Materials division as Solstice Advanced Materials US Inc (Nasdaq: SOLS), which is now the listed contact on county parcel records for this property. The site remains on the EPA National Priorities List (Superfund). Solstice inherited environmental remediation liabilities from Honeywell as part of the spin-off; the Claymont AWE site traces directly to Allied Chemical's fluorine/specialty chemicals operations — the same business that became Solstice. Solstice's SEC filings acknowledge material environmental cleanup obligations. Residents and DNREC should confirm which entity now holds formal legal responsibility for site remediation.

properties.name: Honeywell Delaware Plant
properties.type: Specialty chemicals — CLOSED (plant auctioned/decommissioned; BF3 line transferred to Solstice)
properties.note: Honeywell's Claymont Delaware plant was the sole U.S. manufacturer of boron trifluoride (BF3) and fluorosulfonic acid. AllSurplus conducted a "no reserve" plant closure auction for this Claymont facility, confirming the physical plant has been decommissioned. The BF3 product line transferred to Solstice Advanced Materials (spun off from Honeywell on October 30, 2025; NASDAQ: SOLS), which now markets itself as "North America's leader in boron trifluoride technology." Whether Solstice has restarted production elsewhere is unconfirmed. The Claymont plant site sits adjacent to the AWE Superfund site and adds to the legacy contamination burden in the corridor.

properties.name: Evraz Claymont Steel — Former Steel Mill (closed 2015)
properties.source: EPA TRI / DNREC Title V / DNREC VCP
properties.note: Steel production at this site ended in 2015 after nearly a century of operations. The property and surrounding land remain contaminated with heavy metals, oils, and industrial byproducts from steel manufacturing. The site is subject to ongoing DNREC oversight. Permit violations and hazardous site conditions remain active concerns. Three large distribution warehouses — totaling over one million square feet — have since been built on and adjacent to the former mill property, bringing a new wave of diesel truck traffic and industrial noise to a neighborhood already burdened by decades of heavy industry.

properties.name: Pepsi Distribution Center — Former Steel Mill Site
properties.chemicals: Diesel exhaust (PM2.5, NOx, benzene), Engine noise
properties.note: Large distribution warehouse built directly on the former Evraz/Citisteel steel mill property — land that remains under DNREC oversight for contamination from nearly a century of steel production. Constant diesel truck traffic to and from this facility adds to Claymont's already 96th-percentile traffic exposure burden. Residents were not meaningfully consulted on the reuse of this contaminated industrial land for another high-truck-traffic use.

properties.name: Agile Cold Storage — Former Steel Mill Site
properties.chemicals: Diesel exhaust, Refrigerant emissions (ammonia or HFCs), 24-hr mechanical noise
properties.note: Refrigeration warehouse built on the former Evraz/Citisteel steel mill property. Refrigeration facilities operate 24 hours a day — meaning diesel truck arrivals, refrigeration compressor noise, and equipment vibration continue through overnight hours when residents are trying to sleep. Refrigerants used in cold storage (ammonia or hydrofluorocarbons) carry their own health and climate risks. This site adds a continuous noise and air quality burden on top of the existing industrial legacy of the property.

properties.name: Former Tri-State Mall — Vacant
properties.note: The former Tri-State Mall is currently vacant with no confirmed permits or approved reuse as of April 2026. CC4EJ is monitoring this site given its size and location in an already overburdened community. Any future industrial or high-traffic use of this property would add to a neighborhood already in the 96th percentile statewide for traffic and diesel exposure.

properties.name: First State Crossing — Commercial/Industrial Development (NCC Monitoring)
properties.type: Commercial/industrial development — New Castle County permit monitoring
properties.source: NCC Land Records / NCC Building Permits / CC4EJ monitoring
properties.note: First State Crossing is a commercial or industrial development immediately adjacent to the Knollwood/Worthland residential neighborhood in Claymont. CC4EJ is monitoring this site for any New Castle County building, site development, grading, or land use change permits that could add traffic, noise, truck activity, or pollution burden to a community that is already undercounted in the EJ data. Knollwood, Aniline Village, and Hickman Row — three distinct residential neighborhoods — are all inside a single census block group, meaning their combined environmental burden is already diluted in every permit review tool DNREC uses. Any new industrial or high-traffic use at First State Crossing would compound that burden without triggering the per-neighborhood review it warrants. Check NCC permit portal and parcel records for active applications and approved uses.

properties.name: Citisteel / Phoenix Steel Contamination Site (DE-0046)
properties.note: 343-acre former steel site at 4001 Philadelphia Pike. Steel production since 1917. 7 operable units under DNREC cleanup. Naamans Creek was relocated during operations. Adjacent to Delaware River and I-95/495.

properties.name: INEOS (formerly General Chemical) — Delaware Valley Works
properties.type: Former sulfuric acid plant — CLOSED (EPA RCRA Corrective Action / remediation site)
properties.note: The Delaware Valley Works (DVW) is no longer producing sulfuric acid. General Chemical was acquired by Chemtrade Solutions LLC in 2014, which then sold the South Plant to Drawbridge Claymont, LLC. Both the North Plant (vacant, held by Honeywell/now Solstice) and South Plant are under EPA RCRA Corrective Action. A public meeting was held in April 2024 for ongoing remediation. INEOS has no current operational role at this site. The DVW and adjacent Honeywell/AWE sites form a concentrated contamination corridor along Philadelphia Pike in Claymont — the same corridor where CC4EJ members live and work.

properties.name: I-95 / I-495 / Route 13 — Claymont Diesel Corridor
properties.source: DelDOT AADT 2023; DNREC; CC4EJ listening session
properties.note: Community repeatedly identified being sandwiched between I-95 and I-495 as a primary air/noise concern (Sept. 2025 listening session, 47 attendees)

properties.name: Monroe Energy LLC — Trainer Refinery
properties.source: EPA TRI / EDF CEAM / DNREC VOC Study 2019
properties.chemicals: Benzene, Toluene, SO2, NOx, PM2.5, Hydrogen sulfide, VOCs
properties.de_implication: This refinery processes approximately 185,000 barrels of crude oil per day on the Delaware River, 3 miles from Claymont across the PA state line. DNREC's 2019 VOC Community Study was designed specifically to test whether emissions from this corridor reach Claymont residents. EDF's Chemical Exposure and Action Map (CEAM) identifies it as a major contributor to cumulative toxic exposure along the Delaware River. Delaware residents have no legal standing in PA air permit proceedings for this facility despite breathing the same air.

properties.name: Energy Transfer Marcus Hook Complex
properties.source: EPA TRI / DNREC VOC Study 2019 / CC4EJ listening session Sept. 2025
properties.chemicals: Methane, Propane, Ethylene, Butane, Benzene, VOCs
properties.de_implication: One of the largest LNG export facilities on the East Coast, located directly on the Delaware River in Marcus Hook — the facility most frequently named by Claymont residents as their top air concern at CC4EJ's Sept. 2025 listening session (47 attendees). Flaring events release VOCs and combustion byproducts. PCIST's 20-year cancer study documents Marcus Hook Borough residents — living adjacent to this complex — face laryngeal cancer at 280% above the US rate. Prevailing winds carry emissions northwest toward Claymont.

properties.name: Braskem America — Marcus Hook
properties.de_implication: Braskem operates the largest polypropylene production facility in the Americas at Marcus Hook. 1,3-Butadiene is a known human carcinogen (IARC Group 1) associated with leukemia and lymphoma. The facility is 2.5 miles from Claymont. PCIST cancer data for Marcus Hook Borough — immediately adjacent — shows liver cancer at 168% above the US rate and pediatric liver cancer at 2,362% above the US rate, consistent with long-term exposure to the compounds released at this and nearby facilities.

properties.name: Lubrizol Corp — Pedricktown Plant
properties.de_implication: EDF's Chemical Exposure and Action Map (CEAM) identifies Lubrizol as accounting for approximately 23% of cumulative chemical exposure burden in the Delaware River corridor. Acrylonitrile (IARC Group 2B) and formaldehyde (IARC Group 1 — known human carcinogen) are the primary releases. Formaldehyde is associated with leukemia and nasopharyngeal cancer. These compounds are part of the same chemical burden affecting the airshed serving Claymont, DE, 4 miles across the state line.

properties.name: Valtris Specialty Chemicals — Delaware River Plant
properties.de_implication: Valtris manufactures DEHP and related phthalate plasticizers on the Delaware River in Marcus Hook. DEHP is an endocrine-disrupting compound classified as a probable human carcinogen by EPA and a Substance of Very High Concern under EU REACH. EDF's CEAM tool lists this facility as a named contributor to cumulative toxic exposure in the Delaware River corridor — the same regional airshed as Claymont, DE. Phthalates are associated with developmental and reproductive harm, adding to the cumulative burden on communities along this corridor.

properties.name: ReWorld (formerly Covanta) Chester Incinerator
properties.chemicals: Dioxins/furans, Lead, Cadmium, Mercury, PM2.5, NOx, Hydrogen chloride
properties.de_implication: The largest trash-to-energy incinerator in the United States, burning approximately 3,500 tons of municipal solid waste per day from multiple counties. Chester, PA — a majority-Black city 8 miles north of Claymont — has among the highest cancer rates in Pennsylvania, substantially driven by this facility. Dioxins and furans released during incineration are persistent organic pollutants that travel significant distances, contributing to regional dioxin background levels in the Delaware Valley airshed that affects Claymont and the broader NCC industrial corridor.

properties.name: Evonik Corp — Marcus Hook
properties.chemicals: Hydrogen peroxide, Organic peroxides, Specialty chemical intermediates
properties.de_implication: Evonik manufactures specialty chemicals including organic peroxides at Marcus Hook, PA, 2.5 miles from Claymont. Organic peroxides are reactive oxidizers that contribute to ground-level ozone formation — the same ozone that worsens asthma and lung disease in downwind communities. Claymont residents are breathing air from a corridor where multiple facilities are simultaneously releasing ozone precursors, adding up to a burden no single permit review captures.

properties.name: Mexichem Specialty Resins (Vestolit) — Marcus Hook
properties.chemicals: Vinyl chloride, Ethylene dichloride, PVC resin dust, VOCs
properties.de_implication: EDF's Chemical Exposure and Action Map identifies this facility as a named contributor to cumulative chemical exposure in the Delaware River corridor. Vinyl chloride is a known human carcinogen (IARC Group 1) — the same compound linked to liver angiosarcoma, a rare cancer documented at elevated rates in communities near PVC manufacturing sites. Located 3.5 miles from Claymont in the same industrial cluster that Claymont residents identified as their top air concern.
properties.note: NOTE: The location of this facility (Marcus Hook, PA) is UNCONFIRMED. Research found no current Vestolit/Orbia documentation listing a Marcus Hook PA facility. Confirmed Vestolit U.S. sites were Pedricktown NJ (now closed), Avon Lake OH, and Henry IL. This entry may be a data error or reflect a legacy/traded asset. The Pedricktown NJ Mexichem/Vestolit entry (now also confirmed closed 2024) is the confirmed NJ location. Recommend verification against original EPA TRI source before treating this as accurate.

properties.name: Chemours Chambers Works — Deepwater, NJ
properties.source: EPA TRI / EPA PFAS enforcement / Delaware River Basin Commission
properties.chemicals: PFOA (C8), GenX (HFPO-DA), PFOS, Fluorinated intermediates, HF, VOCs
properties.de_implication: Chambers Works is one of the most significant PFAS contamination sources in the United States and is located directly across the Delaware River from Delaware. For decades, DuPont (now Chemours) released C8 (PFOA) from this plant into air and water — contaminating the Delaware River, which serves as drinking water source for millions including Delaware communities. The Delaware River Basin Commission has found PFAS contamination throughout the watershed. This facility and Chemours Edge Moor in DE (same company) form a two-state PFAS contamination corridor along the river. PFAS are associated with thyroid disease, kidney and testicular cancer, immune suppression, and developmental harm.
properties.note: Still operating as of 2025. Chemours continues to produce fluorinated chemicals (including GenX/Krytox lubricants and fluoropolymer-related products) at this 1,455-acre complex. However, Chemours is actively marketing 230+ acres of surplus land parcels via JLL, suggesting significant rationalization of the site. In August 2025, Chemours, DuPont, and Corteva reached an $875 million settlement with New Jersey (payable over 25 years beginning no earlier than January 1, 2026) to resolve all PFAS and legacy environmental claims tied to Chambers Works and other NJ sites. For decades, DuPont/Chemours released C8 (PFOA) from this plant into air and water — contaminating the Delaware River, which serves as drinking water source for millions including Delaware communities. Chemours is simultaneously expanding PFAS/fluoropolymer production at its Fayetteville, NC plant. Delaware communities served by the Delaware River remain at risk from ongoing and legacy PFAS releases.

properties.name: Paulsboro Refining Company — Paulsboro, NJ
properties.type: Specialty lube oil & asphalt plant (crude/FCC idled Oct 2020; formerly full refinery) (NJ)
properties.chemicals: Benzene, Toluene, Xylene, SO2, NOx, PM2.5, Hydrogen sulfide
properties.de_implication: PBF Energy shut down most of Paulsboro's refining units in October 2020 — including the crude distillation unit, FCC, alkylation unit, and coker — laying off ~250 workers. Since then the facility has operated only its lubricant base oil and asphalt units, making it the East Coast's largest asphalt producer (~11,000+ bbl/day lube base stock) and supplying intermediates to PBF's Delaware City, DE refinery. Air emissions from lube/asphalt operations (sulfur compounds, VOCs, PM) continue, and the facility still holds a Title V air permit. The site sits on the NJ bank of the Delaware River, part of the same river corridor industrial cluster affecting New Castle County, DE. The 2020 idling of crude refining displaced refinery workers in an already overburdened community.

properties.name: LANXESS Corp — Logan Township, NJ
properties.chemicals: Chlorinated organics, Rubber chemicals, Specialty intermediates, VOCs
properties.de_implication: LANXESS operates a specialty chemical facility in Logan Township, NJ, contributing chlorinated organic compounds and VOCs to the Delaware River airshed. Logan Township sits midway between Philadelphia and Wilmington along the NJ shore — its emissions mix with those from PA and DE facilities to create the cumulative chemical burden that no single state's environmental agency has full visibility into. New Castle County, DE is downwind of this corridor under common weather patterns.

properties.name: Infineum USA — Paulsboro, NJ
properties.chemicals: Petroleum distillates, Organic sulfur compounds, Zinc compounds, VOCs
properties.de_implication: Infineum manufactures fuel and lubricant additive packages at Paulsboro, NJ on the Delaware River. Organic sulfur compounds and petroleum distillates released during production contribute to particulate formation and ground-level ozone in the Delaware Valley airshed. Located on the NJ shore directly across from the Marcus Hook/Chester PA industrial cluster — together these two banks of the Delaware form one of the most industrially dense river corridors on the East Coast, with Delaware communities at the downstream end.

properties.name: Chemours Edge Moor (formerly DuPont) — TiO2 / PFAS
properties.type: Former TiO2 chemical plant / PFAS contaminated brownfield — CLOSED 2016
properties.note: Chemours announced closure of the Edge Moor TiO2 plant in 2015 and ceased production by early 2016. The site has been substantially repurposed for port use and renamed "Port of Wilmington – Edge Moor Facility." It is under EPA RCRA Corrective Action for PFAS and legacy DuPont/Chemours contamination of the Christina River and Delaware River. Although no longer manufacturing, this site is historically responsible for decades of PFAS contamination affecting drinking water sources throughout the region. The contamination legacy continues to affect New Castle County communities and downstream water supplies.

properties.name: DSWA Cherry Island Landfill
properties.type: Active solid waste landfill / landfill gas recovery (no active incinerator)
properties.note: The Cherry Island Landfill (1706 E. 12th St., Wilmington DE) is an active municipal solid waste landfill accepting MSW, C&D debris, asbestos, and other materials. It has operated since 1985. Landfill gas is collected and converted to energy. Note: there is NO active MSW incinerator at this site — Delaware closed its last in-state incinerator years ago and now exports waste to out-of-state facilities (primarily the ReWorld/Chester incinerator in Chester PA). The landfill itself is an active air quality concern through landfill gas emissions (methane, VOCs) and heavy truck traffic in an area already burdened by the adjacent industrial corridor.

properties.name: Metachem Products — New Castle (chlorinated solvents site)
Occidental Chemical Corp. — New Castle
properties.type: Former chlor-alkali plant — CLOSED 2005 (EPA RCRA Corrective Action / mercury remediation)
properties.note: The OxyChem New Castle chlor-alkali plant ceased chlorine production in November 2005 and potassium hydroxide production in 2007. Decommissioning and demolition were completed 2007–2008. The site has been under EPA RCRA Corrective Action since a 2012 consent order for mercury, benzene, and volatile organic contamination. Remediation is in its final stages. More than 100 former workers filed mercury exposure lawsuits in 2024. The corporate entity OxyChem was sold to Berkshire Hathaway for $9.7 billion (completed January 2, 2026), but Occidental retains legacy environmental liabilities at this site. Mercury contamination from this plant has affected New Castle Creek and surrounding soils.

properties.name: I-95 / Route 141 Interchange — NCC Industrial Corridor
Dover Air Force Base
properties.source: DNREC / USAF CERCLA / EPA PFAS Site Registry
properties.note: Dover AFB is Delaware’s largest military installation, covering 3,900 acres in central Kent County. The Air Force’s decades-long use of aqueous film-forming foam (AFFF) for firefighting training has caused significant PFAS (per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances) contamination of groundwater beneath and surrounding the base. PFOS and PFOA — both classified as likely human carcinogens by EPA — were detected at levels far above health advisory limits in private drinking water wells near the base perimeter, prompting the Air Force to provide bottled water and point-of-use filters to affected households in the Wyoming and Woodside communities east of the fence line. DNREC enforces Delaware’s PFAS MCLs — among the strictest in the nation at 10 ppt for combined PFOS+PFOA — and monitors contamination plumes extending from the base under its independent authority. The Air Force is conducting investigation and cleanup under CERCLA’s Installation Restoration Program (IRP), with DNREC co-oversight. Kent County’s most significant PFAS exposure risk tracks directly to the base’s AFFF history. The base also generates chronic aircraft noise and ultrafine particle emissions from C-17 Globemaster III operations over surrounding communities.

properties.name: Indian River Power — Millsboro
properties.type: Power generation — CLOSED (coal units retired February 23, 2025)
properties.note: Delaware's last coal-fired power plant permanently retired all coal units on February 23, 2025 — 22 months ahead of the original schedule, enabled by early completion of Delmarva Power transmission upgrades. PJM estimated the early closure saves ratepayers ~$93 million in avoided reliability-must-run fees. A small 16 MW oil-fired peaking unit remains nominally active for grid emergencies. As of early 2026, Delaware Republican lawmakers are pushing to restart the site as a natural gas plant, but NRG (operator) has stated coal restart is not on the table and no natural gas pipeline is within 2+ miles. The site's closure removes a major air emission source from Sussex County but raises questions about site remediation and future land use. Indian River Generating Station, Millsboro, Sussex County, on Indian River Bay. Operated as a coal-burning power plant for decades by Delmarva Power and later NRG Energy (PSEG), this facility burned millions of tons of coal and stored the resulting coal combustion residuals (CCR — “coal ash”) in impoundments adjacent to Indian River Bay. Coal ash contains arsenic, mercury, selenium, lead, and chromium; at unlined sites these heavy metals leach into groundwater and surface water. DNREC-required groundwater monitoring detected multiple exceedances of drinking water quality standards near the ash impoundments, triggering enforcement under both federal EPA CCR rules and Delaware’s stronger state cleanup standards. DNREC and EPA required NRG/PSEG to investigate, monitor, and begin closure of the coal ash impoundments. The coal-fired units were retired in stages through the late 2010s; natural gas peaking units continue to operate. Indian River Bay — a designated shellfish and recreational waterway critical to coastal communities and historically significant to Indigenous peoples — experienced decades of coal ash-related water quality degradation. The surrounding Millsboro area has a significant Hispanic/Latino population facing both industrial agriculture burdens from nearby poultry processing and this legacy power plant contamination.

properties.name: Perdue Foods — Georgetown Processing Plant
properties.source: EPA TRI / DNREC / ProPublica Chicken Checker
properties.note: 20621 Savannah Road, Georgetown, DE. One of the largest poultry processors in Sussex County. Georgetown's population is approximately 50% Hispanic/Latino — many residents immigrated specifically to work in this and other poultry facilities. In January 2025 a hazardous materials incident triggered a shelter-in-place advisory for surrounding neighborhoods. Ammonia refrigeration systems at poultry processors are a recurring acute hazard in EJ communities. Wastewater and air emissions (ammonia, hydrogen sulfide, particulate) are regulated under DNREC NPDES and Title V permits.

properties.name: Mountaire Farms — Millsboro Processing Plant
properties.source: EPA TRI / DNREC / ProPublica Chicken Checker
properties.note: 29106 John J. Williams Highway (Route 24), Millsboro, DE. One of the largest poultry processors on the Delmarva Peninsula. Mountaire's Millsboro complex has faced repeated DNREC enforcement actions for wastewater violations, including a $650,000 consent agreement in 2019 for spray irrigation overflow that contaminated groundwater and surface water near residential areas. Neighbors report chronic odor from the facility and spray fields. The surrounding workforce is predominantly Hispanic/Latino.

properties.name: Mountaire Farms — Selbyville Processing Plant
properties.source: EPA TRI / DNREC / ProPublica Chicken Checker
properties.note: 55 Hosier Street, Selbyville, DE. Poultry processing plant in southern Sussex County, near the Maryland border. ProPublica's Chicken Checker found high-risk salmonella rates on chicken parts processed here more often than at comparable plants — an indicator of production speed and line conditions that also correlate with worker safety and environmental compliance. Selbyville has a significant Hispanic/Latino farmworker population.

properties.name: Allen Harim — Harbeson Processing Plant
properties.note: 18752 Harbeson Road, Harbeson, DE. In April 2021 DNREC required Allen Harim to take corrective action at both its Harbeson and Millsboro plants for environmental violations. The Harbeson facility has faced enforcement for wastewater discharge and odor complaints from neighboring residents. Harbeson Road runs through a mixed rural-residential area where farmworker families live in close proximity to both the processing plant and surrounding poultry grow-out houses.

properties.name: OxyVinyls LP — Pedricktown Plant
properties.source: EPA TRI (ID 08067XYVNYRTE13) / EPA RMP / DOJ consent decree 2006 / EPA CERCLA/EPCRA penalty 2023
properties.chemicals: Vinyl chloride monomer (IARC Group 1), anhydrous ammonia, methyl acrylate
properties.de_implication: OxyVinyls LP (a subsidiary of Occidental Chemical / Occidental Petroleum) operates a suspension PVC resin plant at Route 130 & Porcupine Road in Pedricktown, NJ — one of the top 5 vinyl chloride air emitters in the United States. The facility reported approximately 60,000 lbs of vinyl chloride to EPA TRI in 2021. Vinyl chloride is a known human carcinogen (IARC Group 1) linked to liver angiosarcoma and liver cancer. The facility holds an EPA Risk Management Plan (RMP) covering vinyl chloride monomer and anhydrous ammonia. Enforcement history: (1) 2006 DOJ/EPA Clean Air Act consent decree for LDAR violations — 00,000 NJ civil penalty plus 40,000 lbs/year emissions reduction commitment. (2) May 2023: OxyVinyls released 53.8 lbs of vinyl chloride — above the 1-lb reportable quantity — through building ventilation and failed to immediately notify authorities. Penalized 13,000 under CERCLA §103 and EPCRA §304. Claymont, DE is approximately 4 miles downwind across the Delaware River and has no legal standing in NJ air permit proceedings.

properties.name: Mexichem Specialty Resins / Vestolit (Orbia) — Pedricktown Plant
properties.type: Former dispersion PVC resin plant — CLOSED end of 2024 (NJ)
properties.source: EPA TRI (ID 08067THGNCUSRTE) / EPA consent decree 2014 / Google Maps confirmed: 76 Porcupine Rd, Pedricktown NJ 08067
properties.chemicals: Vinyl chloride monomer (IARC Group 1), methyl acrylate
properties.de_implication: CLOSED: Orbia (parent of Mexichem/Vestolit) confirmed closure of its Pedricktown, NJ emulsion/dispersion PVC plant by end of 2024, with limited contractual commitments potentially extending into Q1 2025. The plant at 76 Porcupine Road was one of the East Coast's significant vinyl chloride air emitters — reporting 36,790 lbs of vinyl chloride to EPA TRI in 2022. Closure removes an active emission source but leaves legacy site contamination concerns. OxyVinyls LP continues to operate next door as an active major vinyl chloride emitter. The Pedricktown community still faces cumulative exposure from the remaining industrial cluster.

properties.name: Depot Connect International (Quala) — Pedricktown Tank Wash
properties.type: Commercial hazardous tank cleaning / RCRA waste handler (NJ)
properties.source: Wastebits facility locator / NJ DEP / OSHA enforcement records / 8A US Route 130, Pedricktown NJ 08067
properties.chemicals: Hazardous liquid waste, RCRA D003 reactive waste, acrylates, latex, paint resins, toxic poisons, odorous compounds
properties.de_implication: Depot Connect International (formerly Pedricktown Tank Wash, operating as Quala #205) is a commercial tank trailer and IBC cleaning facility at 8A US Route 130, Pedricktown NJ. Licensed to accept RCRA D003 reactive waste, acrylates, poisons, and heavily contaminated trailer loads from surrounding chemical facilities including OxyVinyls and Lubrizol nearby. Tank cleaning rinsewater contains residue of previous tank cargo; NJPDES discharge ultimately enters the Delaware River basin. Parent company OSHA record: two workers killed at its Pasadena TX facility in November 2019 from confined-space fume exposure (97,920 OSHA penalty); a third worker fatality at the same complex in December 2023 (10,703 penalty for repeat confined-space violations). The same operations — cleaning chemical tank trailers — are conducted at the Pedricktown NJ site.

properties.name: Corrosion Control Corporation — Pedricktown
properties.type: Industrial tank coating and corrosion control contractor (NJ)
properties.source: NJ DEP License #002196 / USDOT SAFER 907881 / 177 US Route 130, Pedricktown NJ 08067-3612
properties.chemicals: Epoxy resins, VOC solvents (toluene, xylene, MEK, acetone), abrasive blasting media, lead-containing coating waste
properties.de_implication: Corrosion Control Corporation (founded 1968) operates a 7,200 sq. ft. industrial coating facility on a 9-acre property at 177 US Route 130, Pedricktown NJ, adjacent to OxyVinyls, Mexichem/Vestolit, and Depot Connect International. The company applies protective coatings and epoxy liners to large industrial storage tanks, including at nearby chemical facilities. Coating operations involve VOC solvents and surface preparation that can generate RCRA-regulated paint and solvent waste. While not a TRI reporter, it represents one more industrial land use in a small residential community (~424 people) already surrounded by the OxyVinyls vinyl chloride plant, Mexichem PVC plant, Quala hazardous tank wash, Lubrizol specialty chemicals plant, and the NL Industries lead Superfund site.

properties.name: Logan Generating Plant — Former Coal Power Plant / Brownfield
properties.type: Demolished coal cogeneration plant / coal ash brownfield (NJ)
properties.source: EPA GHGP (ID 1001201) / NJ DEP Title V / Global Energy Monitor / NBC10 / Sierra Club NJ / RMI / 76 US Route 130, Logan Township NJ 08085
properties.chemicals: SO₂, NOx, PM2.5, mercury, CO₂, coal combustion residuals (CCR / coal ash)
properties.de_implication: Logan Generating Plant was New Jersey’s last operating coal-fired power plant — a 225 MW pulverized-coal cogeneration facility on the Delaware River in Logan Township, NJ. It operated from 1994 until May 31, 2022, and was demolished by implosion on December 2, 2022. At peak, it emitted over 1.6 million metric tons of CO₂ per year (EPA GHGP); in its final years ~593,000 MT CO₂/year. Coal combustion releases SO₂, NOx, fine particulate, and mercury — all of which traveled downriver toward the Marcus Hook and Claymont DE corridor under prevailing wind patterns. Logan Township hosts a broader Superfund-era industrial cluster: the Chemical Leaman Tank Lines site (EPA NPL) contaminated township groundwater with arsenic, chromium, lead, and mercury, requiring EPA to connect residents to public water in 1987–1995. The current aerial shows the demolished plant footprint with coal ash management ponds still present. Owner Lotus Infrastructure Partners (formerly Starwood Energy) has stated no additional remediation is needed — no independent community verification of coal ash liner integrity has been published. Site is being redeveloped as an 876 MWh battery energy storage system (BESS).

properties.name: DuPont / Chemours Seaford Works — Former Nylon Plant
properties.source: DNREC VCP / EPA TRI / Nanticoke Watershed Partnership
properties.note: Seaford, Delaware (Sussex County). DuPont opened the world’s first commercial nylon manufacturing plant at this Seaford site in 1939, producing nylon-6,6 from hexamethylenediamine and adipic acid for over 75 years. At its peak the Seaford Works employed thousands of workers and defined the economic identity of the city for generations. Industrial wastewater from nylon synthesis was discharged to the Nanticoke River under DNREC NPDES permits; air emissions including ammonia and process solvents were regulated under DNREC Title V. DuPont transferred the site to Chemours in 2015 and the plant closed that year. DNREC has oversight of remediation under the Voluntary Cleanup Program (VCP); groundwater and soil contamination from decades of chemical manufacturing remain under active monitoring. The Nanticoke River — a major Chesapeake Bay tributary and waterway historically significant to the Nanticoke Lenni-Lenape Tribal Nation — received industrial discharges from this site for over 75 years. Seaford’s population is majority Black, and the Sussex County workforce that staffed this plant for generations now lives near the contaminated legacy site. Redevelopment decisions for this large industrial property carry significant EJ implications for surrounding communities.

properties.name: Dover Gas Light — Manufactured Gas Plant (MGP) Contamination Site
properties.type: Former manufactured gas plant / contaminated site
properties.source: DNREC RS / Delmarva Power / EPA MGP site registry
properties.note: Downtown Dover, Kent County. The Dover Gas Light Company operated a manufactured gas plant (MGP) here from the 19th century through the mid-20th century. MGP operations produced coal-derived gas by heating coal in sealed retorts, generating coal tar, benzene, naphthalene, and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) as byproducts. These compounds are persistent carcinogens that seeped into soil and groundwater at the site and can remain for over a century without active remediation. Delmarva Power (Exelon/Pepco Holdings), as the successor utility to the original gas plant operators, is the responsible party under DNREC oversight. The site sits in the St. Jones River corridor in downtown Dover — an area with longstanding lower-income residential neighborhoods. Benzene, a known human carcinogen (IARC Group 1), is a standard contaminant at MGP sites and is commonly found at concentrations orders of magnitude above safe drinking water limits in affected groundwater. Delaware has more than a dozen legacy MGP sites statewide; Dover’s is one of the most centrally located within a populated urban area.

properties.name: I-495 — Edgemoor / NE Wilmington bypass
properties.note: Dedicated commercial-truck bypass around Wilmington. Heavy port + refinery diesel traffic along the Edgemoor / Claymont / NE Wilmington corridor since it opened in 1977.
